edges.description: Organisms that evade local killing persist in macrophage-rich airway and parenchymal niches.
Infected macrophages and recruited lymphocytes organize into chronic granulomatous lesions.
The intracellular macrophage niche gates therapy toward agents that enter host cells.
Bronchiectatic airway injury increases sputum production.
Chronic mycobacterial airway inflammation is coupled to nodular-bronchiectatic radiographic disease.
Persistent granulomatous inflammation can progress into a destructive fibrocavitary tissue-remodeling pattern.
Destructive fibrocavitary remodeling creates the cavitary lung lesions seen in a substantial subset of M. xenopi pulmonary disease cases.
Damaged airways impair local clearance and make the downstream macrophage-rich pulmonary niche permissive for persistent M. xenopi infection.
